question: An agent using both the memory tool and the clear_tool_uses context editing strategy is about to have its oldest tool results cleared as the conversation grows. The team wants to guarantee important findings already written to memory files are never themselves wiped out by the clearing process. What should they configure?
options: A) Lower the trigger threshold so clearing happens more frequently, which prevents any single clearing event from touching memory results
B) Increase the keep value to the maximum allowed, since keep determines which specific tool names are protected from clearing
C) Disable clear_tool_inputs, since that setting alone controls whether memory tool results can ever be cleared
D) Add the memory tool's name to exclude_tools, so its results are never removed during context clearing
correct_answers: D) Add the memory tool's name to exclude_tools, so its results are never removed during context clearing
explanations: Wrong — the trigger threshold only changes how often clearing runs, not which tool's results are exempt once it does run.
Wrong — keep sets how many recent tool use/result pairs survive regardless of tool name; it doesn't protect a specific tool by name the way exclude_tools does.
Wrong — clear_tool_inputs governs whether tool call parameters are cleared alongside results; it doesn't determine whether a named tool's results are protected.
Correct — exclude_tools lets a team name the memory tool so its results are preserved specifically, regardless of when clearing runs.
